description: We are SkyPages, a team passionate about space exploration and creative learning. We aim to make NASA's space missions interesting and easy for school students to understand through an interactive, animated digital flipbook. Our project will explore equipment left on the Moon and Mars, explain its purpose and discoveries, and use storytelling and animations to inspire young minds to learn about space and science.
summary: SkyPages is an interactive, child-friendly storybook website about NASA equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Children turn the pages of a flipbook to meet the Apollo lander bases and Lunar Rovers, and the Mars robots Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Ingenuity and InSight. Each page combines a real NASA photograph, a short story, animation, background music, read-aloud narration and quizzes. SkyPages answers the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars" by turning forgotten machines into characters that school-age learners can meet. It matters because stories make space science memorable and accessible, and they inspire the next generation of explorers.
details:
SkyPages is a free, interactive storybook website that introduces school-age learners to NASA equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars.

What it does: Children turn the pages of a 16-page flipbook. On the Moon they see the Apollo lander bases, footprints, the Lunar Rover and a rover parked for good. On Mars they meet Sojourner, the twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity, the Ingenuity helicopter (shown with Perseverance) and the InSight lander. Every page pairs a real NASA photograph with a short, simple story and a fun fact. Two quizzes and a storyteller activity invite children to draw, write or act out a robot's story.

How it works: SkyPages is a single web page that runs in any phone or computer browser, with no login or install. Pages turn by tapping the left or right side, swiping or dragging, using the arrow buttons or the keyboard. Sound effects and background music are generated in the browser, and a read-aloud button uses the browser's built-in speech so early readers can listen to each page.

Benefits and impact: It makes space history friendly and memorable, supports listening as well as reading, and works on low-cost phones. We hope teachers and families use it, and we plan to add more missions, languages and classroom activities.

Creativity and design choices: We chose a storybook format, page-flip animation, a calm space soundtrack and large, simple text because young learners respond to stories, motion and sound. Facts were checked against NASA mission pages, and every NASA photo is credited on its page.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Web Audio API, Web Speech API, Google Fonts (Fredoka and Nunito), Python and ffmpeg for the demo video.

AI use: This project was built with AI assistance. Claude (Anthropic), a large language model, helped write the code, simplify the text, and create the illustrations (drawn in code), the music and sound effects (generated in code) and the demo video. The narration voice was generated with an AI text-to-speech tool: GOOGLE AI STUDIO. The SkyPages logo was generated with an AI tool: CHATGPT. The project idea and the choice of challenge were made by our team. AI-assisted content is labeled "AI-assisted • made with Claude" in the video and images, "AI-assisted" in the website footer, and in the file metadata. The NASA photographs are real NASA images and are not AI-generated.
